scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: The Chrysler Building is a 1,046-foot-tall (319 m), Art Deco-style supertall skyscraper in the East Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.
scenes.quote: The Chrysler Building is a 1,046-foot-tall (319 m), Art Deco-style supertall skyscraper in the East Midtown neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City, United States.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: It was both the world's first supertall skyscraper and the world's tallest building for 11 months after its completion in 1930.
scenes.quote: It was both the world's first supertall skyscraper and the world's tallest building for 11 months after its completion in 1930.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: The Chrysler Building was designed and funded by Walter Chrysler personally as a real estate investment for his children, but it was not intended as the Chrysler Corporation's headquarters (which was located in Detroit at the Highland Park Chrysler Plant from 1934 to 1996).
scenes.quote: The Chrysler Building was designed and funded by Walter Chrysler personally as a real estate investment for his children, but it was not intended as the Chrysler Corporation's headquarters (which was located in Detroit at the Highland Park Chrysler Plant from 1934 to 1996).

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: An annex was completed in 1952, and the building was sold by the Chrysler family the next year, with numerous subsequent owners.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: In 2007, it was ranked ninth on the American Institute of Architects' list of America's Favorite Architecture.
scenes.quote: In 2007, it was ranked ninth on the American Institute of Architects' list of America's Favorite Architecture.

scenes.title: Overview
scenes.caption: As of 2019, the Chrysler is the 13th-tallest building in the city, tied with The New York Times Building.
